paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's city has room for people nobody expected. The voice in this psalm names Babylon, Philistia, Tyre and Cush, places far outside Israel, and says of each one, "This one was born in Zion." (Psalm 87:4) I think those names would make a crowd gasp, and I would be gasping right along with them.

And look who's doing the counting. The LORD Himself will record it in the register of the peoples, so it's not a rumor or a maybe (Psalm 87:6). The Most High Himself will establish Zion, so nobody gets in or stays in by their own muscle (Psalm 87:5). If you've ever felt like a stranger at the edge of God's people, this psalm says He's the One who writes down who belongs.

So where does that leave you, baker? It leaves you with a spring that never runs dry. The singers and pipers sing, "All my springs of joy are in You." (Psalm 87:7) I spent years in a drawer hunting for joy in all the wrong places, so trust me: go to the real spring, and bring somebody with you!
